summary.intent: Run the GSD phase-orchestration workflow end-to-end for CipherBox Phase 68 (gap-closure planning, execution, and phase completion for ROT-07 rotation UX), then verify the fix by running the full local web-e2e suite, and finally kick off a `/ship-phase` autonomous post-execution loop (verify/secure/validate/simplify/SDK-E2E/CodeRabbit/ship) for Phase 68.
summary.outcome: Phase 68's two gap-closure plans (68-11, 68-12) were planned, executed, and verified passed (14/14 must-haves), but a user-requested full local web-e2e run revealed the app cannot complete login/browse/download/write flows due to 46 pre-existing 'not implemented — phase 63/65' stubs; this led to scoping and fully planning a new Phase 68.1 (14 plans, 6 waves) to wire the read+write runtime, plus a decision to merge Phase 68 to main before starting 68.1. The session ended mid-way through the /ship-phase workflow for Phase 68 (pre-flight done, steps not yet executed) when the user interrupted.

repo: CipherBox v2.0 web app has ~46 'not implemented — phase 63/65' stub throws across packages/sdk/src and apps/web/src covering the entire read-chain (login/root-init, navigation, file preview/download/streaming, shared-folder read) and write-chain (owned file upload/replace/versions, bin re-link, share/invite creation, shared-folder write ops) — full web-e2e cannot pass until these are wired

packages/sdk/src/client.ts ensureFolderLoaded (the SDK-internal resolve fail-closed gate target named in 68-VERIFICATION.md) is dead code that throws 'not implemented — phase 63'; the real live chokepoint for the fail-closed gate is reconcileFolderSequence, called before every rename/delete/deleteToBin/move (client.ts:518, 5 call sites)

packages/sdk-core/src/share/shared-write.ts is the canonical, fully-implemented write-chain reference (createSharedSubfolder, uploadToSharedFolder, updateSharedFile, moveInSharedFolder, deleteFromSharedFolder) — the shared path carries a full write-body model (writeKey/publishedNode) while the owned FolderState (packages/sdk/src/types.ts:164) is read-chain-only with no writeKey/publishedNode, forcing a model extension for owned file writes

SealedChildRef (packages/core/src/node/types.ts) has no 'kind' field by design (v3 schema frozen), so file-vs-folder discrimination requires resolving each child's PublishedNode.kind and caching it — cannot be inferred from the parent's sealed child ref alone

main branch already contains Phases 61-67 merged individually via squash PRs (#578-#586); GSD's branching_strategy: phase forks each new phase branch off origin/main, so an unmerged phase's code would be lost when planning the next phase unless merged first

CI split: ci.yml (PR gate: lint/typecheck/unit) runs on pull_request to main and does NOT include web-e2e; ci-e2e.yml (which runs web-e2e) triggers only on push to main — so a phase can merge to main with web-e2e still red, and web-e2e only validates post-merge

tests/web-e2e Playwright config auto-starts mock-ipns-routing (:3001), API dev (:3000), and web dev (:5173) via webServer; external infra needed is Postgres (:5432), Kubo (:5001/:8080 CORS), Redis (:6379/6380) plus built packages and a built mock-ipns-routing dist
apps/api dev server runs 'nest start --watch' with migrationsRun: true (synchronize off) — a fresh start auto-applies TypeORM migrations, no manual migration step needed

gsd-tools has a 'phase' subcommand supporting decimal phase insertion (e.g. 'phase insert 68' creates Phase 68.1 between 68 and 69 without renumbering later phases) — safer than hand-editing ROADMAP.md

GSD's automated decision-coverage gate fails to parse bold/backtick-formatted 'D-NN' bullets in CONTEXT.md, reporting 0/0 even when decisions are properly covered by plans — a formatting artifact, not a real gap

code.finding: reconcileFolderSequence is the live pre-mutation resolve gate called before renameItem/moveItem/deleteItem/deleteToBin (5 call sites); Phase 68-11 gated it via enforceResolved to make the ROT-07 fail-closed anti-rollback property actually reachable, since ensureFolderLoaded (originally named in VERIFICATION.md) is dead phase-63 stub code

rotateReadFromNode originally discarded the root's rotated {readKey, generation, sequenceNumber} behind a void return; changed to return RotateReadResult | undefined so performScopeExitRotation can refresh folderTree and avoid a same-session post-rotation deadlock until page reload

new-user login throws 'not implemented — phase 63' after SIWE succeeds because root Node initialization (publishing an empty root Node via the Node codec) was never wired — root cause of every web-e2e login-dependent test failing; introduced in Phase 62 commit b2dba554a, not by Phase 68 work

workflow: When a subagent reports a task as 'complete' with a corrected target that deviates from the original spec (e.g. gating a different function than the one named in VERIFICATION.md), independently verify the substitution is sound before trusting it — here both the planner and a separate plan-checker/verifier independently confirmed the named target was dead code, which validated the deviation

Before declaring a phase verified/complete based on subagent reports, distinguish between tests that were actually *executed* vs. specs that were only *authored and registered* (e.g. Playwright --list) — the user caught that 'web-e2e coverage' claims meant registered-not-run, prompting an actual full local run that surfaced a real, large gap

When reusing a running dev server (e.g. 'nest --watch') instead of restarting it for an e2e run, verify it reflects current source/env by hitting a route/endpoint added by the target change (e.g. PATCH /shares/:id/grant returning 401 not 404) rather than assuming freshness from process age alone

Investigate a single anomalous test failure (e.g. one transient 401) before assuming it's the root cause — here the apparent secret-mismatch culprit turned out benign on re-test, and the real root cause was a deeper stubbed dependency (phase-63 stub) revealed by reading the Playwright error-context page snapshot at timeout

AskUserQuestion checkpoints were used appropriately at multiple decision points (auto_advance/interactive config conflict before launching execute-phase; combined vs. split read/write phase framing; before touching branches/PRs) rather than silently proceeding on ambiguous or destructive-adjacent choices

friction: Config conflict discovered mid-run: auto_advance: true and mode: interactive were simultaneously set, requiring a stop-and-ask before auto-advancing into execute-phase on security-sensitive crypto code

GSD's commit-helper produced repeated false-negative 'commit_failed' reports while commits actually landed (edf3c078e, c7974c1ff, others) — required verifying with git log every time instead of trusting the tool output

Reusing existing local infra (docker containers, dev API on :3000) required significant manual triage: an unhealthy mock-ipns container that turned out actually healthy, a stale API process vs. a live nest --watch process that respawned on the same port, and secret-value comparisons across three .env files before ruling out env drift as the failure cause

Playwright's webServer requires BASE_URL=localhost:5173 to auto-start app servers; had to manually verify this wasn't pointed off-localhost before trusting the suite would run the real stack rather than skip server startup

Full web-e2e run took ~22.7 minutes and still mostly failed (6 passed/19 failed/183 not run) due to a single upstream stub blocking nearly the entire login-dependent test surface — expensive way to discover a structural gap that could have been caught by reading the stub count earlier

Automated decision-coverage gate tool couldn't parse the CONTEXT.md bullet formatting, producing a false 0/0 result that had to be manually reconciled against the plan-checker's independent (correct) confirmation

A planner subagent silently renamed/switched the git branch during 68.1 planning (from feat/web-integration-rotation-ux-and-durable-client-state to feat/web-client-runtime-integration), requiring investigation to confirm no work was lost and the split was clean
